stories.new_fact: The Army said its controlled detonation of deteriorating lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant succeeded; reporting described continuing criticism about notification.
stories.new_takeaway: Completion of a disposal operation does not substitute for published sampling methods, results, and follow-up actions.
stories.why_now: The operation and Army statement occurred Friday, within the 48-hour freshness window.
stories.previous_coverage: No comparable Iowa disposal operation appeared in the prior seven episodes.
stories.uncertainty: The report does not establish a final environmental or health outcome; sampling and guidance remain the relevant evidence.
stories.watch: Published environmental sampling, public-health guidance, and any follow-up action.

stories.new_fact: AP reported early Black Friday promotion and AI-tool referral signals while completed holiday sales, returns, and margins remained unresolved.
stories.new_takeaway: Promotional traffic is not a completed-sales or household-affordability conclusion.
stories.why_now: Black Friday reporting is dated Friday and follows the event covered in real time.
stories.previous_coverage: November 27 covered pre-completion Black Friday signals; this follow-up changes the takeaway to waiting for actual revenue and margin evidence.
stories.uncertainty: Third-party traffic and promotion measures do not establish conversion, returns, fraud, margins, or final demand.
stories.watch: Cyber Monday and post-weekend data separating revenue, unit volume, returns, financing use, and margins.

stories.new_fact: Columbus Crew beat Inter Miami 1-0 on a stoppage-time Santiago Rodríguez goal and advanced from the first-round series.
stories.new_takeaway: A completed playoff result and today’s separate Ohio State game should be treated as distinct travel and event-demand inputs.
stories.why_now: The match finished overnight Friday; the initial report was published early Saturday.
stories.previous_coverage: The prior seven episodes did not report this completed series result.
stories.uncertainty: The next playoff opponent, date, and venue require official league or club scheduling confirmation.
stories.watch: Official Crew and MLS confirmation of the next playoff schedule.

stories.new_fact: Freddie Mac reported a 7.21 percent average for the 30-year fixed rate as of November 25, down from 7.28 percent a week earlier.
stories.new_takeaway: The immediate operational task is reconciling live pricing, lock terms, disclosures, and borrower scenarios rather than treating the survey average as an offer.
stories.why_now: Holiday-weekend quiet-day specialist update: the newly checked survey remains operationally relevant to active lock and disclosure workflows.
stories.previous_coverage: November 26 mentioned the rate dip for holiday lock communication; this segment uses a different, transaction-specific takeaway and stays within the permitted dated update exception.
stories.uncertainty: The survey average is not a borrower-specific quote and does not establish an affordability or demand trend.
stories.watch: Next PMMS release, lender lock data, and purchase-file turn-time evidence.
stories.date_exception: The November 25 survey is inside seven days but outside the 48-hour fresh window; it is a single home-lending operational update and does not count toward the four fresh developments.

stories.new_fact: Reporting described Hyundai Card and JPMorgan Kinexys completing a proof of concept in which corporate agents checked balances, compared FX quotes, and prepared conversion and remittance actions within preset authority limits.
stories.new_takeaway: Agent payment experiments should be assessed through identity, authority, escalation, adverse-case, and reconciliation evidence—not an autonomy label.
stories.why_now: The report is dated November 27 and provides a specific financial-services experiment not used in recent episodes.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent episodes covered bank customer-agent terms, evaluation infrastructure, and lending-platform modernization, not this corporate treasury proof of concept.
stories.uncertainty: No production volume, error rate, fraud result, execution-quality baseline, savings, or independent test is disclosed.
stories.watch: Test protocol, identity-control evidence, real-authorized-transaction outcomes, exception handling, and independent assessment.
stories.ledger_row_changed: Added Hyundai Card and JPMorgan Kinexys, lane six treasury and payments experiment, as a proof-of-concept row with no disclosed production metric.

stories.new_fact: Anthropic’s Claude Ship workflow was reported as chaining pull-request review, code fixes, and approval-oriented steps, with published warnings that it may miss bugs or security vulnerabilities.
stories.new_takeaway: A chained coding-agent workflow is a reason to define proposal, merge, and deployment boundaries; it is not evidence of autonomous-release safety.
stories.why_now: Holiday-week quiet-day specialist update: newly uncovered November 23 agent-workflow change, not previously used in the seven-episode comparison.
stories.previous_coverage: The prior seven scripts covered voice, banking controls, healthcare configurations, and model access, but not Claude Ship’s chained PR workflow.
stories.uncertainty: Public reporting provides no independent defect-escape, rollback-cost, security, or regulated-bank production comparison.
stories.watch: External evaluation, disclosed failure cases, customer evidence, and measured post-deployment quality.
stories.date_exception: This November 23 Frontier AI agent-workflow update is newly uncovered and operationally relevant, but it is a dated specialist update rather than fresh-story credit.
stories.frontier_bar: agent and tool-use advance: a chained review-and-fix workflow for code changes.
